Closest prior work: PatchCore, SPADE (memory matching); AnomalyDINO, UniVAD, WinCLIP (few-shot); RegAD, InCTRL, ResAD (cross-category transfer)
Already covered: Few-shot reference matching on natural-object benchmarks is established. Cross-category generalisation exists for natural objects.
Still open: Systematic same-wafer vs cross-wafer vs cross-type evaluation on die imagery; explicit evidence of when transfer fails.
Type of claim: Combination of existing methods + new evaluation protocol

Closest prior work: RegAD (learned registration); GraphCore (rotation invariance); PaDiM (alignment-dependent); classical registration (ECC, Fourier–Mellin); Zontak & Cohen (registration-free)
Already covered: Alignment and invariance for few-shot AD exist. Classical die registration is standard industrial practice.
Still open: Measuring whether alignment or invariance removes or weakens real defects (defect preservation), including orientation-dependent defects; 'warp the reference, not the target' design.

Closest prior work: One-class AD (PatchCore etc.) flags any deviation; DRA (open-set supervised AD); Shin et al. (open-set at wafer-map level); IC-DefectNCD (novel class discovery in IC SEM)
Already covered: Detecting deviations is established; open-set recognition exists at image or wafer-map level; NCD exists on private IC data.
Still open: Pixel-level three-way triage (normal / known class / unknown) driven by normal references plus a small known-defect memory, evaluated with leave-one-class-out on public SEM masks.

Closest prior work: WM-811K line of work (wafer-map pattern recognition); Chen 2020 (die indexing); industrial die-to-die practice
Already covered: Wafer-map pattern recognition is mature; die-image inspection is mature; they are usually studied separately.
Still open: Linking per-die anomaly scores to wafer-level spatial statistics. No public dataset links die images to wafer coordinates, so this can only be tested on synthetic or partner data.

Closest prior work: Abbas et al. 2026 (HITL memory correction, simulated feedback); UCAD (continual AD); Prasad et al., PIRB (continual learning in semiconductors); Cai et al. (active learning)
Already covered: Training-free memory correction from feedback was shown on MVTec AD with clean simulated feedback (preprint).
Still open: Noisy or wrong feedback, quarantine and rollback, contamination and false-positive drift, forgetting on semiconductor data.
